Aggregate a raster to a coarser time step

Source: R/aggregate_time.R
aggregate_time.Rd

Aggregates the layers of a raster by day, month or year, for example hourly ERA5 temperature to daily maxima or daily rainfall to monthly totals. The result's layers are named by the ISO date on which each period starts ("2021-02-01" for February 2021), carry those dates, and record the new time step.

Usage

aggregate_time(x, to = c("day", "month", "year"), fn = NULL, ..., label = NULL)

Arguments

x

A SpatRaster with dates, ideally read with read_climate().

to

Target time step: "day", "month" or "year".

fn

Summary function name passed to terra::tapp(), e.g. "sum", "mean", "max", "min", "modal".

...

Further arguments to terra::tapp(), e.g. na.rm = TRUE.

label

Optional label for the result; defaults to that of x.

Value

A SpatRaster with one layer per period.

Details

When fn is not given it follows from the variable: amounts such as precipitation and evapotranspiration are summed, categorical layers take the most frequent value, everything else is averaged. The choice is announced. Summing a rate per time step gives a rate per new period, so daily "mm/day" summed to months is recorded as "mm/month".

See also

read_climate(), raster_meta()

Examples

pre <- read_climate(
  system.file("extdata", "pre_daily.tif", package = "c4e"))
#> Read pre_daily: pre [mm/day], daily, 2021-01-01 to 2023-12-31, 1095 layers
#> (synthetic).
monthly <- aggregate_time(pre[[1:59]], "month")
#> Aggregating to month with `fn = "sum"`: pre is an amount.
names(monthly)
#> [1] "2021-01-01" "2021-02-01"
